text:
Ty Emberson's value has never shown up on the scoresheet, and this season is no exception: two assists in 21 games at about 12 and a half minutes a night as a right shot on Edmonton's bottom pair.

Last season made the case for him. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 0.4 wins above replacement, nearly all of it from defending at even strength, with opponents getting 0.16 fewer expected goals per 60 when he was out there (89th percentile). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking agreed that offense isn't where he earns his keep.

This season's five-on-five picture is weaker. With Emberson on the ice the Oilers get 37% of the shot attempts and 37% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), 11 points worse than without him. And the scoreboard has been generous: the team has scored 5.3 more goals than those chances deserve during his shifts, the kind of luck that rarely lasts.

So the results look better than the play. If his chances against return toward last season's level, he's a useful depth defenseman for Mike Babcock. If they don't, the bounces are covering for a slide.
